name: Eduardo Telles Gi Octopus Guard System
description: Explore Eduardo Telles Gi Octopus Guard System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Eduardo Telles Gi Octopus Guard System is a study framework for connecting octopus sweeps and back takes while accounting for gi grips.
overview:
A gi grip can change both the available entry and the response to a sweep. Eduardo Telles's Octopus With Pajamas gives this guide a specific gi focus, linking half-guard and closed-guard situations with butterfly-assisted movement and back exposure. Use that narrower brief when comparing it with Craig Jones's no-gi Octopus guide. The aim here is to recognise a few repeatable choices in your existing guard, rather than collect every variation at once.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: The sleeve contact depends on clothing and changes the available connection; it cannot be copied unchanged into no-gi.
The posting choice changes your base and helps explain how the movement is supported.
The partner response may expose their back, but that exposure must still be connected to stable rear control.
Both partners should understand the starting contact and intended direction of movement.
Their grips and body constraints differ, so success in one entry does not show the other is reliable.
Whether the new top position is controlled or the partner can recover before the transition is complete.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Using the gi lesson as a no-gi grip prescription
common_obstacles.solution: Identify which contact depends on clothing before attempting to transfer the drill.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Adding a roll before understanding the base
common_obstacles.solution: Return to the basic sweep and practise the change of weight cooperatively.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Ignoring the partner after the sweep
common_obstacles.solution: Continue only far enough to establish top control or identify the back exposure.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Treating two entry positions as identical
common_obstacles.solution: Record the half-guard and closed-guard results separately.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Half Guard and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.

flashcards.question: Why compare the basic octopus sweep with the elbow-post variation?
flashcards.answer: The posting choice changes your base and helps explain how the movement is supported.

flashcards.question: How can sweep defense influence the decision to follow the back?
flashcards.answer: The partner response may expose their back, but that exposure must still be connected to stable rear control.

flashcards.question: What should be established before adding a butterfly-assisted octopus branch?

products.title: Octopus With Pajamas
products.blurb: A directly matched instructional companion for connecting octopus sweeps and back takes while accounting for gi grips. Review its published contents and sample to judge the teaching approach.
products.best_for: Gi practitioners with a working half guard or closed guard who want a compact introduction to octopus sweeps and back-taking decisions.
products.study_focus: Compare the half-guard sweep with its elbow-post variation, then study the closed-guard sleeve option and the sweep-to-back relationship.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: begin with 'Choose a familiar gi guard' from Half Guard. Record which partner response interrupts the plan and revisit that lesson before adding another branch.
